neutral_facts.value: The accused, a tailor, assaulted his wife and two sons with a pair of scissors, causing their deaths, and inflicted stab injuries on his daughter. He left the daughter in a condition where she survived due to assistance from a neighbor. The accused then went to the police station and reported the incident. The prosecution relied on the daughter's testimony, medical evidence, and recovery of the weapon. The accused denied the allegations during his police statement but did not present any defense evidence. The trial court convicted him of murder and attempted murder, sentencing him to death and life imprisonment respectively.

key_evidence_accepted.value: The appellant suffered from economic and psychic compulsions, including abject poverty, which led him to commit the murders. The key witness, PW1 (the daughter), provided a detailed and consistent account of the incident, corroborated by PW4 (the maternal aunt). The appellant's own statement to the police, where he explained his actions due to financial stress and family suffering, was also accepted as evidence.

quotes.text: It has come in evidence that accused suffered from economic and psychic compulsions

witness_credibility.value: The main witnesses, particularly PW1 (the daughter) and PW4 (the maternal aunt), were found to be credible. Their accounts were consistent and corroborated each other, and PW1's testimony was further supported by medical evidence and the police statement.

quotes.text: PW1-Gaitri alias Pooja was clear and consistent during the investigation as well as before the Sessions Court

post_offence_conduct.value: The appellant went to the police station and reported the incident, indicating cooperation with authorities. He also left the injured daughter in a condition where she could receive medical attention, showing some remorse and attempt to mitigate the consequences of his actions.

quotes.text: He left the child in that condition, bolted the door from outside and went straight to the police station and reported the incident

quotes.text: The trial court convicted the appellant under Sections 302 and 307 IPC and sentenced him to death under the first count and life imprisonment under the second one.
The appeal filed by the appellant before the High Court was dismissed confirming the conviction and sentence under Section 307.

Allowing the appeals in part, the Court HELD: 1.1. Before awarding a sentence of death, in view of s. 354(3), Cr.PC, the court has to first examine whether it is a case fit for awarding of life sentence and if not and only then, the death sentence can be awarded.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused caused the death of his wife and two sons and attempted to cause death of his daughter, and that the trial court's conviction and sentencing were appropriate.

quotes.text: The prosecution examined nine witnesses and based mainly on the version of PW1-Gaitri, the appellant was convicted under Sections 302 and 307.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the accused was suffering from economic and psychic compulsions due to abject poverty and that the case did not fall under the rarest of rare category, thus warranting a lesser sentence.

quotes.text: The possibility of reforming and rehabilitating the accused cannot be ruled out. He had no prior criminal record.
The case does not fall under the rarest of rare category so as to warrant a punishment of death.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that life imprisonment is the rule for murder, and death sentence is the exception, requiring special reasons to be recorded.

quotes.text: The rule is life imprisonment for murder, and death is the exception for which special reasons are to be stated.

Before awarding a sentence of death, in view of s. 354(3), Cr.PC, the court has to first examine whether it is a case fit for awarding of life sentence and if not and only then, the death sentence can be awarded.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: Economic and psychic compulsions, lack of prior criminal record, possibility of reforming and rehabilitating the accused, and the fact that the accused was not likely to be a menace or threat to society.

other_sentence_order.value: The death sentence under Section 302 was commuted to life imprisonment, and the life imprisonment under Section 307 was reduced to 7 years. If the life imprisonment is remitted or commuted to a specified period, the sentence under Section 307 shall commence thereafter.
